'''Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party''' ('''ALCP'''), also known as the '''Cannabis Party''',<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://elections.nz/democracy-in-nz/political-parties-in-new-zealand/register-of-political-parties/|title=Register of political parties {{!}} Elections|website=elections.nz|access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref> is a [[political party]] in New Zealand. It is dedicated to the legalisation of [[Cannabis (drug)|cannabis]] for medical, recreational and industrial use.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://policy.nz/2023/party-vote/parties/aotearoa-legalise-cannabis-party |title= Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party |website= policy.nz |access-date= 28 October 2023}}</ref> It was founded in 1996 and has stood in every general election since, but has never won representation in Parliament. Several of its members have gone on to political success after leaving the party.

==Party history==

=== Cannabis in New Zealand ===
{{See also|Cannabis in New Zealand}}
Cannabis is the most widely used illegal drug in New Zealand.<ref name="ndp">{{cite book |last= |url=http://www.health.govt.nz/system/files/documents/publications/national-drug-policy-2007-2012.pdf |title=National Drug Policy 2007–2012 |publisher=Ministerial Committee on Drug Policy; Ministry of Health |year=2007 |isbn=978-0-478-30751-1 |location=Wellington |access-date=9 February 2017}}</ref> Its use today is regulated by the [[Misuse of Drugs Act 1975]], which classes it as either a Class B drug ("Very high risk of harm") or a Class C drug ("moderate risk of harm"), depending on the product or substance. In December 2018, the Misuse of Drugs act was amended allowing for much broader use of medical marijuana, making the drug available to terminally ill patients in the last 12 months of life.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=Ainge Roy|first=Eleanor|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/dec/11/new-zealand-passes-laws-to-make-medical-marijuana-widely-available|title=New Zealand passes laws to make medical marijuana widely available|date=2018-12-11|work=[[The Guardian]] |location=London|access-date=2018-12-11|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Also in December 2018, the Government announced a non-binding referendum on cannabis for personal use, to be held as part of the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 general election]],<ref name="Referendum-RNZ">{{cite news|url=https://www.radionz.co.nz/news/political/378523/binding-referendum-on-legalising-cannabis-for-personal-use-to-be-held-at-2020-election|title=Binding referendum on legalising cannabis for personal use to be held at 2020 election|date=18 December 2018|access-date=18 December 2018|publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]] }}</ref> though the final result was against legalisation.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-07|title=Legal bid underway to dismiss cannabis referendum result|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/cannabis-referendum/300177354/legal-bid-underway-to-dismiss-cannabis-referendum-result|access-date=2021-01-05|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] }}</ref>

=== Party foundation and actions ===
The Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party was founded on 30 May 1996.<ref name=":1" /> [[Michael Appleby (politician)|Michael Appleby]] led the party from 1996 until standing down in 2013.<ref name=":5" /> Currently the ALCP is co-led by Maki Herbert and Michael Appleby, with Steven Wilkinson as its president.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Welcome to the Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party|url=http://alcp.org.nz/about|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115030240/http://alcp.org.nz/about|archive-date=2020-01-15|access-date=13 August 2020|website=ALCP.org.nz}}</ref>

The ALCP has contested all eight general elections held since its founding, as well as all twelve by-elections.<!-- As of the 2017 general election and the Northcote 2018 by-election --> The party has never won representation in [[New Zealand Parliament|Parliament]].

In 2008, the party invited Dunedin South MP [[David Benson-Pope]] to join the ALCP, but he declined, saying, "Their judgement has obviously been impaired by their recreational habits".<ref name="ODT_9280">{{cite web|author=Mackenzie, Dene|date=12 June 2008|title=Party makes MP offer he can refuse|url=http://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/9280/party-makes-mp-offer-he-can-refuse|access-date=3 November 2011|work=[[Otago Daily Times]]}}</ref>

== Policies ==
The ALCP's policies all relate to cannabis, hemp, or drug education.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cannabis.org.nz/policy|title=Cannabis Party Policy|access-date=22 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161228085037/https://cannabis.org.nz/policy|archive-date=28 December 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> These include legalising possession, growing and use of cannabis for those over 18, creating a 'medpot' card, taxing companies involved in the cannabis industry, removing the need for a licence to grow hemp, and funding drug education and research.

== Members' success outside of ALCP ==
Two ALCP candidates went on to become Members of Parliament for the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green Party]]. [[Nándor Tánczos]] and [[Metiria Turei]] were both ALCP candidates in 1996; Tánczos became a Green MP in 1999 and Turei became a Green MP in 2002. Another ALCP candidate, [[Tim Shadbolt]], has been elected mayor in two places; prior to running for ALCP in 1996 he was mayor of Waitemata from 1983 to 1989 and mayor of Invercargill from 1993 to 1995, and afterwards he became the mayor of Invercargill from 1998 until 2022.

Former president and deputy leader [[Abe Gray]] founded [[Whakamana Cannabis Museum]], New Zealand's first and only cannabis museum, and has been a high-profile cannabis activist and protester for decades.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MacManus|first=Joel|date=2020-10-24|title=How Abe Gray became New Zealand's 'Gandalf of Weed'|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/cannabis-referendum/123184117/how-abe-gray-became-new-zealands-gandalf-of-weed|access-date=2021-02-22|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|last=NORML|date=25 September 2013|title=Grand opening for New Zealand's first Cannabis Museum {{!}} Scoop News|url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/AK1309/S00827/grand-opening-for-new-zealands-first-cannabis-museum.htm|access-date=2021-02-22|publisher=Scoop|location=New Zealand}}</ref> Gray is now a member of [[The Opportunities Party]] (TOP). TOP's policy on legalising cannabis has been praised by the president of [[NORML New Zealand]], Chris Fowlie.<ref>{{cite news |last= Noller |first= Geoff |date= 5 July 2017 |title= Cannabis policy: Too important to be left to the politicians? |url= https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/94326397/cannabis-policy-too-important-to-be-left-to-the-politicians |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |access-date= 26 June 2023}}</ref>

The ALCP has nominated candidates for electorate seats in each election since its foundation. No ALCP candidate has ever won a seat.

Their best general election result was in the [[1996 New Zealand general election|1996 election]], where it won 1.66% of the party vote. It won 1.10% of the party vote in 1999, but since then the ALCP has not received more than 1% of the party vote in any election.

The ALCP has also contested many by-elections. Its most successful result was in the [[2004 Te Tai Hauauru by-election]]. Only the [[Māori Party]], the ALCP, and independents contested this by-election. The ALCP candidate, [[Dun Mihaka]], finished second behind Māori Party leader [[Tariana Turia]], receiving 197 votes (2.52%) to Turia's 7,256 (92.74%).
